sections.html:
Layton is Davis County's largest city and the ninth largest in Utah, on the northern Wasatch Front roughly 25 miles north of Salt Lake City and 15 miles south of Ogden. Residents numbered 81,773 in 2020, with an estimate of 85,308 for July 2025. Hill Air Force Base sits on the northern edge, and Clearfield, South Weber, Kaysville and Syracuse are the neighbors.

The east side climbs toward the foothills and Adams Canyon, the middle follows the I-15 corridor with its shopping and hotels, and the west side runs flatter toward the lake wetlands. Housing went up in waves tied to base employment and commuter growth, so one street can mix 1960s ramblers with 1990s homes and newer subdivisions. Condition varies a lot from block to block.

Lake-effect snow and hot summers are hard on roofs and furnaces. An aging one tends to surface in a buyer's inspection, and that is often the moment an owner decides between repairing and selling as is.

sections.h2: Hill Air Force Base and moving on a schedule
sections.html:
The base opened as Hill Field on November 7, 1940, and became Hill Air Force Base on February 5, 1948. It is one of the biggest employers in Utah, and assignments, deployments and retirements create regular turnover in local housing.

An owner who must move by a fixed date, such as after a transfer, can struggle to line that up with a listing that may sit for weeks. A cash buyer can often work to a closing date the seller picks.

Retail and hospitality cluster around I-15, including Layton Hills Mall, a stretch of chain restaurants called Restaurant Row and the Davis Conference Center. East Gate Business Park and a Weber State University campus add jobs and a student population.

I-15 runs through the center of Layton with interchanges at Antelope Drive, Hillfield Road and Layton Parkway. US-89 follows the eastern edge near the foothills, SR-193 runs east and west past the base's south gate, and SR-177 serves the western side. FrontRunner commuter rail stops at Layton Station, where the old Union Pacific depot stood, and Utah Transit Authority runs buses. Homes close to the station or an I-15 ramp appeal to commuters headed for Salt Lake City or Ogden.

Davis School District serves the city. Layton High School opened in 1966 and Northridge High School in 1992, and the Northern Utah Academy for Math, Engineering and Science is an early college charter school partnered with Weber State. Buyers often ask which school boundary a house sits in, so confirm the address with the district instead of repeating a listing description.

Layton code enforcement runs through the police department and focuses on exterior conditions. A violation can slow a sale if a buyer or lender notices it, and unpaid abatement costs can follow the owner.

Code itemLayton requirement
Weeds and grass12 inches or shorter
Junk, appliances, tires, building materialsNot stored outdoors unless fully inside a structure with walls and a roof
VehiclesLicensed, operable and parked on a hard surface; registration expired four months or more means removal or enclosure
Trees and bushesTrimmed to at least 7 feet above sidewalks and 13 feet 6 inches above streets

The usual process starts with a 14-day courtesy notice. After a re-inspection, a Notice of Ordinance Violation can go to the City Attorney's Office. If an owner never cleans up, a judge can order the city to remove the violations and bill the owner plus an administrative fee.

An owner of a vacant or inherited house who lives elsewhere may miss these notices. Reach the department at codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov or (801) 497-8300 to ask whether anything is open on a property.

sections.h2: Valuation notices and the appeal window
sections.html:
Each year at the end of July, Davis County sends out the Notice of Assessors' Property Market Valuation, and appeals close in mid-September. The office can give you the exact day before you file.

Appeals are heard by the Davis County Commission acting as the Board of Equalization. They can dispute market value but never the tax rate, and the filer must be the owner or an agent holding notarized authorization. Strong support is closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales near January 1, or documented errors in the assessor's data.

Visit Tax Administration at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, call 801-451-3331 or write taxadmin@daviscountyutah.gov. If you bought recently, the price on your closing statement backs up a value discussion.

sections.h2: What happens to the primary residence exemption?
sections.html:
Utah removes 45 percent of the market value of a primary residence, leaving 55 percent taxable. The home must be occupied at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and a household can claim only one such exemption.

A sale or deed transfer ends the exemption for the old owner. The new owner files Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and counties are barred from taking late applications. Amended Utah Code 59-2-103.5 requires owners to file that form in certain situations starting January 1, 2027.

Sellers feel this mainly through how a buyer reads the numbers: a house taxed at 55 percent of value can jump to 100 percent for a year if the new owner files late. Tell your buyer about the form.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Layton house work?
sections.html:
Title work in a cash sale looks like any other sale, without the mortgage approval. You sign a purchase contract, a title company searches for liens, and the Davis County Recorder in Farmington records the deed.

  1. Tell us the address, the house's condition and any deadline, such as a base transfer or a code notice.
  2. Look over the offer and the proposed closing date.
  3. Sign the contract while the title company clears liens, unpaid property taxes and open code charges.
  4. Sign the deed at closing, and the proceeds reach you after payoffs.

Davis County runs a Property Watch email alert that tells an owner when a title on a parcel changes. If you live away from Layton or inherited a house, sign up to hear about any change.

Before closing, collect the deed, your latest tax notice and any letters from code enforcement. If a lien or an open violation turns up in the title search, the title company will tell you what must be paid or cleared and will deduct it from your proceeds. Ask for the settlement figures a day ahead so you know the final amount, and keep copies of every signed page.

faqs.a: Layton is the largest city in Davis County. The 2020 census counted 81,773 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 85,308.

faqs.q: Does Hill Air Force Base affect Layton home sales?
faqs.a: Yes, indirectly. The base borders Layton and is one of the largest employers in Utah, so moves and retirements regularly bring owners who need to sell or buy on a set schedule.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property tax valuation notices mailed?
faqs.a: At the end of July each year. The appeal deadline falls in mid-September, so confirm the exact date with the Tax Administration office at 801-451-3331.

faqs.q: Can code enforcement notices be fixed before selling a house in Layton?
faqs.a: Yes. Layton starts with a 14-day courtesy notice, and many items such as weeds, junk or an inoperable vehicle can be cleared in that window. Email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov to ask what is open on an address.

faqs.q: Does a buyer keep the primary residence exemption on a Layton house?
faqs.a: No, not automatically. New owners must file Form TC-473A by September 15 to receive the 45 percent exemption, and a late filing can mean being taxed at full market value for that year.
